{"explanation": "{\"explanation\": \"Hello! Come, today let us look at a very important and interesting family in chemistry. \\n\\nOnly the elements present in **Group 2** in the Periodic Table are called by us as **\\\"Alkaline Earth Metals\\\"**.\\n\\nTo understand this very simply, let us look at it as some notes:\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 1. Who and all are there in this family?\\nThere are a total of 6 members (elements) in this family:\\n1. **Beryllium (Be)**\\n2. **Magnesium (Mg)**\\n3. **Calcium (Ca)**\\n4. **Strontium (Sr)**\\n5. **Barium (Ba)**\\n6. **Radium (Ra)** *(This is a radioactive element)*\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 2. Why did the name \\\"Alkaline Earth Metals\\\" come to these?\\nTwo meanings are hidden in its name itself:\\n* **Alkaline (Base):** When the oxides of these metals dissolve in water, they form **basic/alkaline (alkaline natured)** solutions (that is, their pH value will be above 7).\\n* **Earth (Soil):** In ancient times, chemists called substances that did not melt easily by heat and were obtained as minerals in the Earth's crust as \\\"Earths\\\" (soil). \\n\\nOnly because these two joined together, these are called **\\\"Alkaline Earth Metals\\\"**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 3. Their \\\"super power\\\" and important properties (Properties):\\n\\n* **Valence Electrons:**\\n  In the outermost orbit of all the elements in this family, only **2 electrons** will be present ($ns^2$). In order to attain stability (Stability), easily giving away these 2 electrons to others, these will turn into **ions having a +2 charge ($M^{2+}$)**.\\n  \\n* **Appearance:**\\n  To look at, these will be in a silver-like white color, and shiny. These are somewhat harder than the alkali metals (Group 1 - Sodium, Potassium).\\n\\n* **Reactivity:**\\n  These will react with the oxygen in the air, and with water. But, they will not explode very aggressively to the extent of Group 1 (alkali metals); they possess a somewhat moderate reactivity.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 4. Where are these used in our daily life?\\nOnly if it is known where what is read in the book is in real life will it be interesting, right? Here are some examples:\\n\\n* **Calcium (Ca):** Only calcium is the reason for the bones and teeth in your body to be strong! Calcium is also present in the slaked lime we apply to betel leaves and in the whitewash applied to walls.\\n* **Magnesium (Mg):** Magnesium is present in the 'chlorophyll' (Chlorophyll) that helps plants do photosynthesis (Photosynthesis). A bright white light comes when firecrackers burst, right, that is only due to magnesium!\\n* **Strontium (Sr) & Barium (Ba):** Strontium is used for a **red color** to come in Diwali firecrackers, and barium is used for a **green color** to come.\\n* **Radium (Ra):** This is a historically significant radioactive element that was used in cancer treatment (discovered by Madam Marie Curie).\\n\\n---\\n\\n### To remember in brief:\\n> **Group = 2**  \\n> **Valency = 2**  \\n> **Ion formed = +2 ($Mg^{2+}, Ca^{2+}$)**  \\n> **Character = Alkaline nature + Being obtained in the earth.**\\n\\nI hope now you have understood clearly about alkaline earth metals. If you have any doubt in this, feel free to ask!\"}"}
